calls.headline: CIB's nine-month profit edges up to EGP 63.1bn; core growth 18%
calls.body: CIB's consolidated net profit for January to September rose 1.6% to EGP 63.1bn from EGP 62.1bn, the bank told the exchange on Tuesday (Mubasher Banks, Fintechgate). Third-quarter profit fell 17.4% to EGP 23.8bn from EGP 28.8bn, because last year's quarter held a one-off EGP 13.1bn provision release; the bank puts underlying nine-month growth at 18%. Net interest income rose 18.6% to EGP 93.3bn and deposits 30.5% this year to about EGP 1.45tn. The net interest margin was 8.02% in the quarter against 8.40% for the nine months, return on equity 38.3% in the quarter, and bad loans 1.47% of the book, covered 343% by provisions. Management targets EGP 80–85bn for 2026 (Al Ahly Pharos via Al Mal).
calls.view: In line, not a beat: EGP 63.1bn leaves about EGP 17–22bn for the fourth quarter to meet guidance, below the third quarter's EGP 23.8bn, so the target looks safe. The quarter's narrower margin reflects 825 basis points of cuts through February, before the October 29 hike, which only helps from the fourth quarter. At EGP 128.05 the stock trades at about 4.8 times the last 12 months' earnings and 1.5 times book; with the results risk gone, the desk expects it to hold the EGP 120s and lead the EGX30 into the December rate meeting.
calls.wrong: CIB closes below EGP 118 before the end of November.

calls.headline: Inflation slows to 12.7%, leaving rates 7.3 points above prices
calls.line: A wider real-rate cushion pays foreign bill holders to stay, but core prices picked up.
calls.body: Annual urban inflation slowed for a third month to 12.7% in October from 13.9%, its lowest since January, and the nationwide rate to 12.0% from 12.8% (EnterpriseAM, Amwal Al Ghad); JPMorgan had forecast 13.8%. Monthly prices rose 0.7%. Core inflation eased to 13.1% a year but rose 1.2% in the month from 0.8%, and JPMorgan sees headline back at 14.3% by December as the base effect fades. The deposit rate is 20% and the one-year bill cleared at 26.03% on November 5.
calls.view: The print removes pressure for another hike and leaves Egypt paying one of the highest real yields among emerging markets, which supports the pound and bank margins. A cut on December 17 is unlikely with core prices speeding up month on month and the Fed leaning to a hike; expect a hold. Food and consumer names see little relief: poultry and cooking oils each rose 7.4% in the month.
calls.wrong: Thursday's 364-day bill clears below 24.5%, a sign markets price early cuts, or the central bank cuts on December 17.

calls.headline: Locals carry a 1.19% EGX30 rise as foreigners sell EGP 303m
calls.line: The busiest session in the log came without foreign money, the open view's main support.
calls.body: The EGX30 rose 1.19% to 51,414.93 on Monday on EGP 10.1bn of turnover. Egyptians bought a net EGP 347.8m while foreigners sold EGP 302.8m and Arabs EGP 44.9m (Masrawy; Vetogate gives EGP 302.9m and 44.4m); Egyptians made up 90.1% of trading. e-finance and Juhayna rose 5.1% each, Cleopatra 4.2% and Telecom Egypt 3.3% to EGP 134.00, a sixth straight gain before Thursday's results, while Abu Qir fell 2.7% to its lowest since August. The EGX70 EWI rose a fifth session, by 1.54%.
calls.view: Local money is rebuilding positions after October's margin calls, and that can keep small caps rising, but the rally lacks the foreign buying the desk's EGX30 view rested on. The index sits about 2% below its 50-day average of about 52,470; expect it to hold above 49,256 through Thursday, with Telecom Egypt's results the near test.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 49,255.66 by November 12.

calls.headline: Evergreen returns to Suez as container transits run 26% above last year
calls.line: The canal's recovery is now in the data, and an Iran deal would speed it.
calls.body: Taiwan's Evergreen sent its first ship through the canal in nearly three years on Sunday, the last Ocean Alliance member to return (EnterpriseAM). Container ships averaged 13.4 transits a day in the week of October 12, against 10.6 a year earlier, while all transits rose only about 1% to 44.3 a day (IMF PortWatch); October toll receipts rose 94% to $724m. President Trump called the Iran war "effectively over" militarily (Al Jazeera), and Brent fell 5.85% to $92.57. Houthi missiles were intercepted over Riyadh on Tuesday. Alexandria Containers rose 3.0% to EGP 33.13.
calls.view: Bigger container ships coming back raise revenue per transit, which is why receipts nearly doubled while ship counts barely moved; that is a steady new dollar source for the pound and volume for Alexandria Containers. A settlement that reopens Hormuz would add to it. The risk is the Houthis turning from Saudi targets back to ships.
calls.wrong: Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping resume, or Alexandria Containers closes below EGP 29.

calls.headline: October CPI decides whether Monday's 2.35% rebound holds
calls.body: October consumer prices are due at 8:30am New York time, forecast at 3.9% a year from 3.7% in September, with 0.3% on the month and 0.2% for core. Fed funds futures price about an 84% chance of a quarter-point hike on December 9. The S&P 500 rose 2.35% to 7,549.94 on Monday, recovering most of last week's losses (Reuters), the VIX fell to 19.92 from 25.64 on Friday (Cboe), and the 10-year yield closed at 4.88%. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said last week that inflation "has moved in the wrong direction" since March.
calls.view: Monday priced relief, not a soft print: with a hike near certain, the market needs CPI at or below 3.9% to keep the rebound. A core reading above 0.3% would push yields toward 5% and hit the most expensive stocks first; a print near 3.6% would extend the rally into chips. The desk leans to a print in line and a choppy week, not a new leg up.
calls.wrong: CPI comes in under 3.6% and the 10-year yield falls below 4.60% by Friday.

calls.headline: Nvidia falls to an April low as chip stocks surge 6.9%
calls.line: Investors kept the AI trade but moved away from Nvidia's key-person risk.
calls.body: Nvidia fell 4.3% to $178.67 on Monday, its lowest close since April and 25% below its 52-week high, after its board opened an independent inquiry into whether Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence; Huang says he will cooperate fully (Al Jazeera). Chip stocks rose 6.9%, led by Broadcom's 8.8% to $319.48, and AMD rose more than 10% on a Google deal and an analyst upgrade. Shareholder lawyers filed a class action in California (TechCrunch). Results are due November 17.
calls.view: The selling is about governance, not demand, which is why the rest of the sector rallied. That keeps Nvidia capped until the inquiry ends or results reassure, and it helps Broadcom and AMD as buyers diversify. The desk's chip view, judged Friday, is on track with Nvidia far below $220.
calls.wrong: Nvidia closes above $210 before its results on November 17.

calls.headline: Brent slides 5.85% on Iran talk; Exxon signs a Venezuela memorandum
calls.line: Cheaper oil caps energy stocks; Venezuela is a long-dated option, not this year's profit.
calls.body: Brent settled at $92.57 on Monday, down 5.85%, after President Trump said Iran was "effectively over" militarily (Al Jazeera), and traded near $91 on Tuesday. Exxon signed a preliminary agreement with Venezuela's PDVSA to assess producing and new fields (Reuters, teleSUR); no investment figure was given. Exxon fell 0.7% to $164.77, 12% below its 52-week high of $187.25 and below its 50-day average of about $170.
calls.view: Oil is pricing an end to the war, and the US blockade of Iranian ports still stands, so a deal could push Brent lower again; that weighs on Exxon's near-term cash flow more than Venezuela adds. Energy stays a laggard while talks continue.

calls.headline: Visa says US payment volumes have sped up to about 10%
calls.line: Card spending is still accelerating, a support for payments and retailers.
calls.body: Visa's finance chief told Citi's fintech conference on Monday that US payment volumes, 6–8% for the past 18 months, recently reached about 10%, and that October trends were stable. Value-added services revenue topped $14bn, up 30%, and should grow in the low-to-mid 20s percent in fiscal 2027 (Investing.com transcript). Visa closed at $422.42, about 31.8 times the last 12 months' earnings.
calls.view: Faster nominal spending is good for Visa's volumes and for Walmart and Costco, but it is also the kind of number that keeps the Fed hiking. Visa's services growth makes it less tied to the cycle than the volume figure suggests.
calls.wrong: Visa closes below $395 by the end of November.

view.headline: Real rates near 7 points keep the dollar in EGP 53–55
view.body: October's 12.7% inflation against 26% bills pays foreign holders well to stay, the dollar index fell 0.6% on Monday, and cheaper oil eases the import bill, so the pound has room to hold near EGP 54. The risks are a hot US inflation print today that lifts the dollar, core prices rising 1.2% a month, and fertilizer export earnings lost to gas cuts.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before the end of November, or Thursday's bills clear well below 24.5%, a sign of early rate cuts.
